replying_to: Replying to Learning to Disentangle Textual Representations and Attributes via Mutual Information

content.title: Recommendation to Reject
content.review:
Summary:

The paper proposes a novel variational upper bound estimation of the mutual information (MI) between an identified attribute and the latent vector, which can be used as an additional objective to improve the disentanglement of representations. The authors suggest replacing the KL divergence surrogate for MI with α-Renyi divergence with higher orders to make the disentanglement more effective. They provide results of a bunch of numerical experiments using fair classification and sentence generation tasks.

Pros:
- The paper is well written and structured.
- The proposed variational upper bound looks carefully formulated.
- The authors provide detailed theoretical proofs and analysis of proposed MI surrogates in Supplementary Materials.
- The paper also considers the case of multi-class scenarios, the topic which is usually omitted in such researches.

The main concern:

- The paper shows as a proposed objective leads to almost complete vanishing of attribute information from the latent vector by the price of huge loss in terms of content preservation metrics (BLEU). The examples of generated texts given in Supplementary Materials show the same: the resulting text usually has a little in common with the original one. 
- However, this effect can be achieved by the following extreme baseline: put random values into the latent vector, then produce one of the fixed, remembered by the decoder target class outputs -- this is a kind of a model overfitting, giving the high Accuracy and Fluency scores while losing in BLEU.
- Moreover, despite the important observation given in Lample et al. (2018) about the difficulty of attainability a completely disentangled latent representation between the content and attributes, there are practical examples of additional objectives which can be used to improve disentanglement while keeping the high BLEU score (check, for example [arXiv:1909.12928]). 
- Thus, the results of the paper don't prove the usefulness of the proposed approach in terms of reaching the good disentanglement _and_ keeping the content information unchanged at the same time.

Minor comments:
- I find the charts with a couple of very different overlapping markers a bit hard to read.
- Figure 3,4,5: X-axis labels are mixed.
- Cosinus Similarity -> Cosine Similarity.
content.rating: 4: Ok but not good enough - rejection
content.confidence: 3: The reviewer is fairly confident that the evaluation is correct

content.title: Mutual information has been used before
content.review:
This paper proposes to use mutual information instead of the more popular adversarial approaches to disentangle representations of text for classification and generation tasks. The paper provides empirical comparisons between multiple versions of their model and a baseline that uses adversarial loss.

However, mutual information has already been used for disentangling representations . A simple Google search outputs [1] and [2], and while the paper did cite the latter, it is only mentioned once in the Introduction and the paper has not done any concrete comparison between these methods and the proposed one. What are the main differences between these previous work and the method proposed in this paper? Please detail this in the paper and if possible, include empirical comparisons with these previous methods as well.

[1] https://www.aclweb.org/anthology/2020.acl-main.673.pdf

[2] https://arxiv.org/pdf/1912.03915.pdf
content.rating: 4: Ok but not good enough - rejection
content.confidence: 2: The reviewer is willing to defend the evaluation, but it is quite likely that the reviewer did not understand central parts of the paper

content.title: This paper presents a method to learn  disentangled textual representations  by minimizing a variational upper bound of the mutual information between an identified attribute and the latent code of a deep neural network encoder.
content.review:
This paper presents a method to learn  disentangled textual representations  by minimizing a variational upper bound of the mutual information between an identified attribute and the latent code of a deep neural network encoder. Experimental results on fair classification and sentence generation tasks show that the new method leads to better disentangled representations on while not suffering from the degeneracy of adversarial losses in multi-class scenarios. 

Theorem 1 is quite straightforward to obtain, where it just apply KL divergence on the entropy and Renyi divergence on conditional entropy. The authors state that "Eq. 6 shows that the cross-entropy loss leads to a lower bound (up to a constant) on the MI. ", but this is in general not true since Y is not uniformly distributed. 

To evaluate the performance of sentence generation, I think an important aspect is missing, which is the diversity as illustrated in the paper by Massimo Caccia, Lucas Caccia, William Fedus, Hugo Larochelle, Joelle Pineau, Laurent Charlin, Language GANs Falling Short, ICLR 2020. The authors should consider the diversity  and compare the results by MLE with temperature sweeping and see how disentangled representations affect both quality and diversity.

Typo: on page 3, last line, "In Sec. 5, we illustrate theses" these
